title: Has anyone actually modeled the EV of fading martingale bots, or does fee drag kill it?
author: Awkward-Telephone581
selftext:
Most leaderboard "quant" bots on public copy-trading boards are just disguised martingale or grid scripts. They print a smooth 90% win rate until one trending candle wipes the whole equity curve.

Logically, if a bot has a guaranteed ruin probability over a long enough horizon, taking the exact opposite side should be +EV. I was initially going to rig up a quick Python script via binance or bybit APIs to scrape and fade the most over-leveraged leaderboard accounts, but didn't feel like babysitting webhooks for a meme experiment. Ended up tossing $50 into bydfi recently just because they have a built-in reverse copy toggle (plus high-water-mark profit sharing for normal copy, which filters out some of the spam). Currently running $25 mirroring a boring low-drawdown swing setup and $25 fading an aggressive high-ROI scalping bot since they don't charge profit split on inverse trades.

The catch I'm already seeing with the inverse test: if the bot spams 40 micro-entries a day, spread and taker fees eat you alive before the big blow-up candle even happens. Has anyone here backtested fading retail grid/martingale bots live, and how do you filter for the ones that are about to nuke?
